confounds.name: Random-seed variability
confounds.detail: Apparent gains may be due to favorable seeds or small-sample noise.

confounds.name: Architecture/capacity differences

confounds.name: Unreliable off-policy evaluation
confounds.detail: OPE can be high-variance/biased, overstating performance.

confounds.name: Normalization/metric bias
confounds.detail: Choice of normalization (random/expert references) or use of maximum-over-training can bias comparisons.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report raw returns alongside normalized scores; avoid maximum-based summaries; use median for multi-game suites.
evidence: An Optimistic Perspective on Offline Reinforcement Learning

Reproducibility of Benchmarked Deep Reinforcement Learning Tasks for Continuous Control

confounds.name: Dataset-collection dependence
confounds.detail: Success may hinge on specific data sources (expert-like, single policy) rather than general algorithmic robustness.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate across datasets differing in quality and collection policies (random/medium/expert/mixed; subsampled/early-stage).
evidence: An Optimistic Perspective on Offline Reinforcement Learning
D4RL: Datasets for Deep Data-Driven Reinforcement Learning
RL Unplugged: Benchmarks for Offline Reinforcement Learning.

confounds.name: Restart bias
confounds.detail: Restarting failed runs for one method inflates stability/performance.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use a no-restart protocol (or identical restart rules) across methods.
evidence: Stabilizing Extreme Q-learning by Maclaurin Expansion

confounds.name: Optimizer choice explains gains
confounds.detail: Switching optimizers (e.g., RMSProp→Adam) can account for improvements.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Include optimizer-matched baselines (e.g., DQN(Adam)) and compare.
evidence: An Optimistic Perspective on Offline Reinforcement Learning

confounds.name: Ensembling/averaging alone explains improvements
confounds.detail: Benefits may arise from variance reduction of ensembles, not the proposed objective.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare to naive/averaged ensembles under identical settings.
evidence: An Optimistic Perspective on Offline Reinforcement Learning

confounds.name: Offline policy selection optimism
confounds.detail: Using online interactions for model selection inflates offline RL performance.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report both online and offline selection protocols; prioritize offline-compatible selection.
evidence: RL Unplugged: Benchmarks for Offline Reinforcement Learning.

confounds.name: Partial observability (lack of memory) causing failures
confounds.detail: Poor results may stem from not modeling temporal dependencies.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use sequenced datasets and recurrent models where applicable.
evidence: RL Unplugged: Benchmarks for Offline Reinforcement Learning.

confounds.name: Reward rescaling artifacts
confounds.detail: Scaling rewards can destabilize or artificially boost training.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Run reward-scale sweeps (with/without normalization) and report sensitivity.
evidence: Benchmarking Deep Reinforcement Learning for Continuous Control
Deep Reinforcement Learning That Matters
Reproducibility of Benchmarked Deep Reinforcement Learning Tasks for Continuous Control

confounds.name: Large uncontrolled policy updates
confounds.detail: Apparent gains may come from overly large parameter steps causing transient improvements.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure mean KL between successive policies; compare to trust-region methods.
evidence: Benchmarking Deep Reinforcement Learning for Continuous Control

confounds.name: Q-value overestimation / miscalibration
confounds.detail: Inflated Q-values can mislead algorithm selection and claimed improvements.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Assess correlation of learned Q with true returns; report Q MSE/overestimation statistics.
evidence: Behavior Regularized Offline Reinforcement Learning
Offline RL Without Off-Policy Evaluation

confounds.name: Determinism exploited by scripted policies
confounds.detail: High scores can be achieved by replaying scripts in deterministic settings.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Introduce environment stochasticity (e.g., sticky actions) during evaluation.
evidence: Gotta Learn Fast: A New Benchmark for Generalization in RL

confounds.name: Local optima/survival bonuses masquerading as success
confounds.detail: Agents may exploit reward structure (e.g., survive without real task progress).
confounds.ruled_out_by: Qualitatively inspect behaviors and trajectory lengths in addition to returns.
evidence: Deep Reinforcement Learning That Matters

confounds.name: Implementation/codebase differences
confounds.detail: Different codebases for the same algorithm can change results.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare multiple implementations under matched hyperparameters.
evidence: Deep Reinforcement Learning That Matters
Reproducibility of Benchmarked Deep Reinforcement Learning Tasks for Continuous Control

experiment_recipes.dataset: D4RL (Gym-MuJoCo locomotion, AntMaze, FrankaKitchen, Adroit, Flow, CARLA, Maze2D) (train)
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: On-policy simulator rollouts for evaluation — Prefer direct environment rollouts over off-policy evaluation estimators for reporting final performance.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On HalfCheetah-medium-v2, Hopper-medium-v2, Walker2d-medium-v2: Random policy normalized D4RL score ∈ [−5, +5] on each task AND Behavior Cloning normalized D4RL score ≥ (Random + 20) on each task. Additionally, on HalfCheetah-expert-v2, Hopper-expert-v2, Walker2d-expert-v2: Behavior Cloning normalized D4RL score ≥ 80 on each task. Failure of any clause refutes.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Cheap sanity check that normalization and evaluation are wired correctly and that trivial baselines behave as expected before heavier tests.

experiment_recipes.goal: Standardized multi-seed evaluation harness ready (shared architecture; 100 eval episodes; ≥10 seeds)
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Shared policy architecture across algorithms — Use the same network sizes/activations for compared algorithms.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: For SAC and TD3 on HalfCheetah-v2, Hopper-v2, Walker2d-v2: (1) Total trainable parameter counts differ by ≤ 5% between algorithms; (2) Evaluation episodes per seed equals 100 (±0); (3) Number of distinct random seeds configured is ≥ 10. Any violation refutes apparatus readiness.
constraints_not_enforced: Exact training budget/frames not standardized across algorithms
experiment_recipes.rationale: Ensures fair, reproducible comparisons by enforcing identical capacity and sufficient evaluation sampling and seeds.

experiment_recipes.goal: Multi-seed norm yields stable SAC vs TD3 rankings on MuJoCo
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Multiple random seeds — Run at least 5 seeds and report mean ± std; use 10 seeds for key comparisons or seed-variance analysis when feasible.
metrics: Statistical significance tests (t-test / KS-test / bootstrap CI) (higher_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Train SAC and TD3 with shared architectures for 1, 5, and 10 seeds; evaluate with 100 episodes/seed. Pass if: (A) Using 10 seeds, for ≥2 of {HalfCheetah-v2, Hopper-v2, Walker2d-v2}, the bootstrap 95% CI of (mean_return_SAC − mean_return_TD3) excludes 0; AND (B) When repeatedly sampling a single seed 1,000 times per task, the fraction of samples whose sign(mean_return_SAC − mean_return_TD3) disagrees with the 10-seed sign is ≥ 30% on ≥2 of the 3 tasks. Otherwise refute.
depends_on: Standardized multi-seed evaluation harness ready (shared architecture; 100 eval episodes; ≥10 seeds)
experiment_recipes.rationale: Directly tests the norm that ≥5–10 seeds are required, by showing single-seed conclusions are unstable while 10-seed comparisons are statistically decisive.

experiment_recipes.goal: Offline selection protocol validity on D4RL (BRAC vs BCQ/BEAR/REM)
experiment_recipes.dataset: D4RL (Gym-MuJoCo locomotion, AntMaze, FrankaKitchen, Adroit, Flow, CARLA, Maze2D) (train)
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Held-out task split for tuning — Tune on a designated subset of tasks within a domain and report final results on disjoint evaluation tasks.
metrics: Statistical significance tests (t-test / KS-test / bootstrap CI) (higher_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Tune hyperparameters for BRAC, BCQ, BEAR, REM on {HalfCheetah-medium-v2, Hopper-medium-v2}; freeze them; evaluate on {Walker2d-medium-v2, HalfCheetah-random-v2, Hopper-random-v2, Walker2d-random-v2, HalfCheetah-expert-v2, Hopper-expert-v2, Walker2d-expert-v2} with 10 seeds and 100 eval episodes/seed. Additionally run an online-selection upper bound per method using extra simulator interactions for selection only. Pass if: (1) For each method, the aggregated (mean across eval tasks) offline-selected score is ≥ 85% of its online-selected aggregated score; AND (2) Method ranking under offline selection matches online selection on ≥ 80% of eval tasks (agreement fraction ≥ 0.8). Otherwise refute.
constraints_not_enforced: Exact offline dataset sizes may vary; only disclosed, not fixed
experiment_recipes.rationale: Verifies the norm that offline-compatible selection with held-out tasks yields robust, not over-optimistic results and preserves method ordering.

experiment_recipes.goal: Sticky-action Atari evaluation stabilizes rankings (QR-DQN vs DQN)
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Environment stochasticity for generalization benchmarks — Enable sticky actions/frame-skip stochasticity to prevent determinism exploitation in ALE/Retro-style evaluations.
metrics: Median normalized score across games (Atari aggregation) (higher_better)
Statistical significance tests (t-test / KS-test / bootstrap CI) (higher_better)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Evaluate DQN and QR-DQN on 26+ ALE games with sticky actions (p=0.25), 10 seeds, 100 eval episodes/seed; also evaluate with no sticky actions and 1 seed. Pass if ALL hold: (A) Under sticky actions (10 seeds), the 95% CI of the difference in median human-normalized score (QR-DQN − DQN) excludes 0; (B) Without sticky actions and 1 seed, ≥ 20% of games show a drop of ≥ 20% in QR-DQN human-normalized score when re-evaluated with sticky actions; (C) Rank agreement (Kendall tau) between two independent 5-seed sticky-action evaluations is ≥ 0.8, while under no-sticky 1-seed it is ≤ 0.6. Otherwise refute.
constraints_not_enforced: Full 57-game suite not required; minimum 26 games
depends_on: Standardized multi-seed evaluation harness ready (shared architecture; 100 eval episodes; ≥10 seeds)
experiment_recipes.rationale: Controls for determinism exploitation and tests aggregation/stochastic-evaluation norms that are standard for ALE-style benchmarks.
